name: Shipping agents and port services
shape_facts: Services offered: line agency, port/husbandry agency, stevedoring, CFS, empty depot, crew services, bunkering coordination.
Ports covered and number of vessel calls or containers handled per month.
Principals: shipping lines, ship owners, charterers, NVOCCs.
Team: boarding officers, documentation, equipment control, accounts, customer service.
How disbursements are funded (principal advance vs agent funds first).
Systems: line’s own system, Excel, email, port community systems, Dubai Trade/PSW.
scope_rule: pi notes operational and business problems: vessel call coordination, document turnaround, DO release, equipment and empty container control, detention/demurrage billing, disbursement accounts, collections, customer service, staff workload and reporting. It does not advise on maritime law, charter party terms, laytime calculations as legal disputes, sanctions, P&I or cargo claims, crew immigration or port safety rules. It never helps release cargo improperly, hide sanctioned vessels or cargo, or pay officials to speed things up. It records principals and customers as roles; never stores crew names, passports, seafarer IDs, or personal details.

vocabulary.line agent: represents a shipping line’s commercial and documentation side locally
vocabulary.port/husbandry agent: handles a vessel’s needs during a port call
vocabulary.PDA / FDA: proforma / final disbursement account of port call costs
vocabulary.detention / demurrage: charges for keeping containers beyond free time
vocabulary.CFS: container freight station where LCL cargo is stuffed/unstuffed
vocabulary.IGM / manifest: import general manifest listing cargo on the vessel

problems.phrase: DO release queue at our counter is always full
Customers can’t see their detention charges until they come to pay
Detention invoices are calculated by hand and often wrong
Empties aren’t returned and we lose track of containers
Equipment imbalance — empties pile up here and are short elsewhere
Principals pay FDAs late and we fund port costs
Disbursement accounts take weeks to finalise
Port invoices arrive after we’ve closed the FDA
Manifest corrections take too long and cause penalties
Boarding officer updates come by phone and get lost
Every customer emails for the same arrival information
Principal’s system and our accounts never match
Staff shifts at port don’t cover night vessel arrivals
Experienced documentation staff leave and new ones make mistakes
Customers dispute detention, saying they returned the box on time
Collections from local customers are slow
Approval of waivers on detention goes through too many people
I can’t see vessel calls, revenues and costs per principal in one view
Principals complain about our KPIs and reporting
Losing an agency principal would hit us hard and I can’t see warning signs
Cash payments at the counter are risky and hard to reconcile
Port charges and tariffs change and our quotes go out of date

do and counter: How does a customer get a DO today, start to finish?
Where do they wait the longest?
detention: How are detention charges calculated and shared with customers?
How often are they disputed, and why?
equipment: How do you track where each container is — with customer, depot, port?
How do you find boxes that are overdue?
disbursements: How long does an FDA take to close after the vessel sails?
cash: Who funds port costs first, you or the principal?
How long do principals take to settle?
vessel calls: How do boarding officers and the office share updates?
principals: What do principals ask you to report, and how do you produce it?
staff: What happens on night or holiday vessel calls?

seasons: Shipping agents follow global trade peaks: August–October before Western Q4, and the pre-Chinese New Year rush, with slack after CNY. In Pakistan, export seasons (textiles, rice, kinnow, mango) shift equipment demand; Eid holidays close offices but vessels still call, creating staffing pressure; Karachi monsoon and cyclone season (May–June, October–November) can disrupt port operations. In the UAE, Ramadan shortens office hours while port operations continue; summer heat affects port labour. In Canada, winter weather on the east coast and the St Lawrence, and rail congestion inland. Global disruptions (route diversions, port congestion) change vessel schedules suddenly.
care: Maritime law, charter party disputes, laytime claims, P&I and cargo claims: legal; pi notes only the operational effect.
Sanctions screening of vessels, cargo, owners or destinations: out of scope; pi does not help work around it.
Crew changes, visas, shore passes: immigration; pi notes only the coordination effort and never stores crew details.
Port safety incidents, injuries, fires, spills or medical emergencies on board: pi stops and points to emergency services and port authorities.
Releasing cargo without proper authority or “managing” officials: pi declines.
Customer and principal financial details: never stored.
build_ideas: Online DO request and payment flow with document upload and status messages, reducing counter visits.
Detention/demurrage calculator per container with live free-time countdown, shared with the customer on WhatsApp.
Container movement tracker (gate out, with customer, returned to depot) with overdue alerts.
Equipment balance view by port and type to support repositioning decisions.
PDA/FDA builder that collects port invoices as they arrive and shows what’s still outstanding.
Principal receivables tracker with ageing and settlement status.
Vessel call board: ETA, berth, boarding updates, tasks and responsible staff.
Automatic arrival notices to consignees from the manifest.
Waiver approval workflow with reasons and limits by role.
Principal KPI report pack produced from the operational data.
Counter cash log with daily closing.

exchange.text: We are agents for two lines in Jebel Ali. Our biggest problem is detention disputes — customers say they returned the empty earlier than our record.
That puts you in a tough spot with customers. Noted. Where does your record of the empty’s return date come from today?
The depot sends us an Excel every few days.
Noted — return dates come from a depot Excel every few days. When a customer disputes, what proof can they or you show?
